extracted.intended_audience: Current and prospective peer reviewers for The BMJ (clinicians and researchers asked to review manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_short: BMJ peer review for research and analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers asked to assess manuscripts for The BMJ, covering expectations about signing reports, declaring competing interests, what to evaluate (originality, importance, reliability, relevance), open peer review practices, and procedural requirements (eg, protocol submission for trials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign reports and declare competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask reviewers to sign their reports and declare any competing interests on any manuscripts we send them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signed reports are part of The BMJ's open peer review policy; reviewers should disclose any financial or non-financial competing interests when returning reviews so editors and readers can assess potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review / prepublication history
rubrics_metrics.description: For research papers and analysis articles, The BMJ has fully open peer review: every accepted research paper submitted from September 2014 onwards and every accepted analysis article submitted from February 2016 onwards will have its prepublication history posted alongside it on thebmj.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prepublication history comprises all previous versions of the manuscript, the study protocol for research papers (see protocol rule), the report from the manuscript committee meeting, the reviewers’ signed comments, and the authors’ responses to all the comments from reviewers and editors. If you experience adverse events from open peer review or want to tell your views, email papersadmin@bmj.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess importance, originality, and reliability (help prioritise)
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask reviewers to help us prioritise the manuscripts that we receive, bearing in mind that The BMJ aims to publish original, important, and reliable articles that will help our readers around the world - who are mainly doctors - to make better decisions about practice, policy, education, and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing, focus on whether the work is original, whether it addresses an important problem, whether the results are reliable and robust, and whether the paper will be useful to The BMJ's clinical and policy readership. Constructive critiques that help editors assess importance and originality are particularly valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive critique to aid editorial decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The best reviews (those that constructively critique the article and help editors assess its importance and originality) are rewarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, specific, actionable feedback that explains strengths and weaknesses, suggests improvements, and separates major issues (eg, validity of methods, conclusions overstated) from minor points (eg, wording, formatting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and act on ethical concerns per BMJ transparency policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The BMJ transparency policy pulls together many separate editorial policies; it's there, for example, that you'll find advice on what to do if you are concerned about the ethics aspects of a manuscript we have asked you to review or if you suspect plagiarism, duplicate publication, or scientific fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suspect plagiarism, duplicate publication, fraud, or other ethical problems, follow the steps in the BMJ transparency policy and raise concerns to the editors rather than handling them solely in your report to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check study protocol for research papers (protocol submission rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prepublication history includes the study protocol for research papers (submitting the protocol is mandatory for all clinical trials and encouraged for all other studies at The BMJ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clinical trials, expect a protocol to be available and use it to check prespecified outcomes, deviations from protocol, and analytic plans. For other studies, seek protocols if provided to assess selective reporting or post hoc analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to review invitations via the online editorial office
rubrics_metrics.description: If we need your help with appraising a manuscript we will email you and ask you to accept or reject the reviewing invitation at our online editorial office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly accept or decline invitations so editors can secure alternative reviewers if needed. Use the online system to submit reviews and manage deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers advise; editors make final decision (and usual review numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers advise the editors, who make the final decision (aided by an editorial manuscript committee meeting for some articles, including original research). Manuscripts sent for review are usually seen by at least two reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame comments to assist editorial judgment rather than to be the final arbiter; be aware that editors may convene a committee meeting and will consider multiple reviews when making decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient reviewers evaluate importance and relevance to patients
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to peer review, we also ask patient reviewers for their opinion on the importance and relevance of selected manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When provided, consider patient reviewers' comments on relevance, burden, acceptability, and clarity of implications for patients; editors may weigh these views alongside technical peer reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality may be eligible for CME credit
rubrics_metrics.description: For the best reviews (those that constructively critique the article and help editors assess its importance and originality) we offer, in partnership with the Cleveland Clinic Foundation, up to 3 AMA PRA Category 1 Continuing Medical Education (CME) points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality, timely, and constructive reviews are eligible; reviewers should consult the BMJ for details on claiming CME credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of provenance added to accepted articles
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of every accepted editorial, research article, clinical review, practice article, analysis article, feature, and head-to-head article The BMJ will add a statement explaining the article's provenance. The options are: Not commissioned; externally peer reviewed; Not commissioned; not externally peer reviewed; Commissioned; externally peer reviewed; Commissioned; not externally peer reviewed; Commissioned, based on an idea from the author; externally peer reviewed; Commissioned, based on an idea from the author; not externally peer reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provenance statement informs readers about whether a paper was externally peer reviewed and whether it was commissioned; reviewers should be aware that their reviews may be linked to these provenance statements in the journal record.
